pull_requests.title: fix(ci): do not keep the job token after checkout (T-035)
pull_requests.description:
Closes #35

  Arnica's scan of main (Day 16) reported four Medium findings: actions/checkout
  left the job token in .git/config in all four workflows. This sets
  persist-credentials: false on each checkout step and adds a check that fails
  when a checkout step does not set it.

  - Workflows: five added lines, nothing else changed.
  - New check: scripts/checkout-credentials.ts, with tests. Red first on the four
    lines Arnica reported.
  - npm run check: 384 pass.
  - Qodo local review: four deep reviews, five findings fixed in three rounds,
    nothing new at the last one.

  Open:
  - Qodo finding d6f052b6 (BACKLOG row says "planned"): by design. The row is set
    to "done (PR n)" in the second commit, so ticket-link is red until then.
  - The two agent workflows are not run by this PR. Unverified until a labelled
    ticket and an agent comment have each pushed successfully.
  - This PR is inside the approval guard (.github/workflows/**, scripts/**):
    prediction, no "Qodo approved" label even when the review is clean.

  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pull_requests.title: ci: pin every workflow action to a commit SHA (T-034)
pull_requests.description:
Closes #32

Every `uses:` in `.github/workflows/` now names a full commit SHA with its release in a comment
(`actions/checkout` v5.1.0, `actions/setup-node` v5.0.0, `anthropics/claude-code-action`
v1.0.283). `@v1` of `claude-code-action` had moved 14 times since the bot's last run, and that
code runs with the Anthropic key and write tokens.

- `scripts/action-pins.ts` + `tests/action-pins.test.ts`: fails closed on any other spelling of
  the `uses` key (human decision after local review 2).
- Repository setting `sha_pinning_required` turned on (with the human's approval): GitHub itself
  refuses an unpinned action. The test is the early warning. Checked first: no lane breaks.
- `AGENTS.md`: the pinning rule; a pin bump is its own human-read pull request.

**Merge order:** merge this before #33. With the setting on, the unpinned workflows on `main`
no longer run, so `check` on `main` would fail after any other merge.

## Day 14 prediction (written before any PR review)
This PR changes files under the Qodo approval guard `.github/workflows/**`.
Expected: **no "Qodo approved" label and no qodo-bot approval**, even if Qodo's complete review of
the head has no Medium+ finding. The guard takes precedence over the workflow
"tracenotes gate: no Medium+ findings → Qodo approved label"; the PR waits for a person.
`check` (Linux, Windows) and `ticket-link` stay separate required checks.

## Local gate
Four deep Qodo reviews, three fix rounds (`evidence/day14/t034/`): 2 Low → fixed; 2 Medium + 2 Low
→ fixed by failing closed; 1 High (5fa32f55, escaped key) → fixed test-first, still listed by the
reviewer with an unchanged description; accepted by the human as "fixed, reviewer stale"
(AGENTS.md gate point 7). `npm run check`: 355 tests.

`ticket-link` is red until the follow-up commit adds the BACKLOG row `done (PR n)`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pull_requests.title: ci(agent-ticket): force tag mode with track_progress so the agent get…
pull_requests.description:
The first automated run on issue #4 reported success after 19 turns with no branch, no
  comment, and no commit. Passing a `prompt` put claude-code-action in agent mode, which does
  not fetch the issue, create a branch, post a tracking comment, or allow git add/commit/push.
  Our prompt told the agent to read the issue it was triggered from, and it had neither the
  issue number nor a tool to get it.

  Changes:

  - `agent-ticket.yml`: `track_progress: true` forces tag mode on issue events. Tag mode fetches
    the issue, creates the `agent/issue-<n>-<slug>` branch, posts a progress comment, allows the
    git commands, and appends our prompt as custom instructions.
  - `agent-ticket.yml`: `Edit` and `Write` removed from the allow-list. Tag mode already permits
    edits inside the workspace; listing them would allow writes anywhere on the runner.
  - Both workflows: `actions/checkout@v5` and `actions/setup-node@v5`, clearing the Node 20
    deprecation warning.
  - `journal/day-04.md`: run log for the three attempts (zombie run during the GitHub Actions
    incident, missing Claude GitHub App, the agent-mode no-op) and what each needed from a human.

  No product code changes.

generated_descriptions.short_why: The initial automated issue run falsely reported success without creating a branch, posting progress, or making any commits because the workflow was using agent mode instead of tag mode. pull_requests.title: ci: required checks, ticket-link check and ticket guard (Day 10)
pull_requests.description: ci: required checks, ticket-link check and ticket guard (Day 10)

generated_descriptions.short_why: This PR was created to enforce required CI on pull requests, prevent ticket-linked PRs from missing the proper issue-closing and backlog update paperwork, and ensure agent-driven ticket work only starts after an investigation has been documented.
generated_descriptions.short_how: Added new GitHub Actions workflows for required checks and ticket-link validation, updated the agent ticket workflow to require an Investigation section and fail early if it is missing, and revised AGENTS.md and BACKLOG.md to codify the new process requirements. Also added Day 10 evidence/context files documenting the change.
generated_descriptions.long:
This PR adds the Day 10 CI and ticket-guarding lane for the repository’s “factory” workflow, covering both automated checks and the paperwork rules around ticket-linked pull requests.

### Why this was created

The change addresses three gaps in the previous process:

1. **No required CI checks were running on pull requests**
   - Before this PR, there was no GitHub Actions workflow enforcing `npm run check` on PRs.
   - That meant “green” status depended on whatever had been run locally, and tests were only effectively validated in limited environments.

2. **Ticket pull requests were not being validated for proper closing/linking paperwork**
   - A prior PR showed the problem: the PR body used `(#20)` instead of a proper closing keyword like `Closes #20`, so the issue stayed open.
   - The backlog entry was also not updated correctly to the expected `done (PR <number>)` format.
   - This PR adds an automated check to prevent that from happening again.

3. **The agent lane could start without the ticket investigation being documented**
   - The workflow that picks up labeled issues now requires the issue body to already contain an `Investigation` section.
   - This ensures the ticket has been checked against the code before the agent starts implementing it.

There’s also an explicit quality-gate note in `AGENTS.md` that the required checks must pass on the PR head commit before merge.

### What changed and how it was implemented

#### New CI workflow for required checks
- **Added** `.github/workflows/check.yml`
- This workflow:
  - Runs on **pull requests** and on **pushes to `main`**
  - Executes `npm ci` and `npm run check`
  - Runs on **both Linux and Windows** using a matrix job
  - Uses read-only permissions only
  - Adds concurrency behavior so PR updates cancel older in-progress PR runs, while main-branch pushes do not get canceled

This creates the required baseline verification for code changes.

#### New ticket-link validation workflow
- **Added** `.github/workflows/ticket-link.yml`
- This workflow runs on PR events, including:
  - `opened`
  - `reopened`
  - `synchronize`
  - `edited`

It validates pull requests that are ticket-related by checking that:
- the PR title includes the ticket id pattern (`T-NNN`)
- the PR closes the ticket’s own issue
- the `BACKLOG.md` entry for that ticket is marked as `done (PR <number>)`

It uses a head-commit checkout so the workflow checks the PR’s own content rather than whatever is currently on `main`.

#### Ticket investigation guard for the agent workflow
- **Modified** `.github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml`

The agent workflow now includes a pre-flight step that:
- reads the issue body from GitHub
- checks that the issue contains a non-empty `Investigation` section
- fails early if the section is missing or empty
- removes the `ready-for-agent` label if the ticket is invalid, so re-adding the label can retrigger the workflow
- comments back on the issue with instructions for fixing the ticket body

The workflow comments and inline documentation also now clarify that:
- the issue body is read at runtime, not at label time
- the ticket must not be widened if code contradicts the investigation
- the final agent comment must mention the required ticket-link paperwork for PRs

The workflow file also includes updated guidance about the optional Qodo review step and the final status message expected from the agent.

#### Repository process documentation updates
- **Modified** `AGENTS.md`

The agent instructions now describe:
- that `src/cli.ts` is the only code under `src/` allowed to directly touch process streams or exit codes
- that factory scripts under `scripts/` may touch process streams only in their entrypoint blocks
- that ticket work requires an `Investigation` section before implementation
- that ticket PRs must close their own issue and update `BACKLOG.md`
- that the following required checks must pass before merge:
  - `check (ubuntu-latest)`
  - `check (windows-latest)`
  - `ticket-link`

This makes the new workflow expectations part of the project’s operating rules.

#### Ticket template update
- **Modified** `BACKLOG.md`

A new required `**Investigation.**` section was added to the ticket format, describing what was checked against the code before implementation and making it explicit that the label workflow will not start without it.

#### Evidence artifacts
- **Added** `evidence/day10/gapfix-context-1.json`
- **Added** `evidence/day10/gapfix-context-2.json`
- **Added** `evidence/day10/gapfix-context-3.json`

These files document the planning, decisions, review findings, and constraints behind the Day 10 work. They appear to be review/context artifacts rather than runtime code.

### Areas/modules affected

This PR affects several parts of the repo:

- **GitHub Actions workflows**
  - `.github/workflows/check.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/ticket-link.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml`

- **Project operating rules / agent instructions**
  - `AGENTS.md`

- **Ticket and backlog process**
  - `BACKLOG.md`

- **Review/evidence documentation**
  - `evidence/day10/*`

### Summary

In short, this PR turns the Day 10 process into an enforced CI + ticket workflow:

- PRs must pass required automated checks
- ticket PRs must close the right issue and update the backlog correctly
- labeled issue tickets must already include a documented investigation before the agent starts

That tightens both code quality and ticket hygiene, and it prevents the kinds of merge-time and labeling errors that had slipped through before.

Day 4: automate the factory's first job.

  - `.github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml`: adding the label `ready-for-agent` to an issue runs
    claude-code-action with a fixed prompt. The agent reads AGENTS.md and the issue, implements,
    runs `npm run check` (three attempts), and commits on `agent/issue-<n>-<slug>`. Guard rails:
    max 40 turns, 30-minute timeout, one run per issue. It does not open the PR; a human does.
  - `.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml`: an `@claude` comment on a PR pushes fixes to that branch
    for Qodo re-review.

    when stdin is a terminal). Mirrored as issue #4.
  - `tickets/T-003`: grouping ticket, written on Day 3, not yet implemented.
  - `AGENTS.md`: process rule amended. Bot commits are allowed only on `agent/*` branches created
    by the workflow; a human opens the PR and merges.
  - `journal/day-04.md`: skeleton with trigger design, run log to follow.

  No product code changes. `npm run check` unaffected.

generated_descriptions.short_how: Added a new `.pr_agent.toml` to disable ignoring bot PRs and bot commit pushes for both `[github]` and `[github_app]`, and expanded `journal/day-04.md` with the full timeline, evidence, lessons learned, and the remaining manual step that was needed before the config change.
generated_descriptions.long:
## Summary

This PR updates the Day 4 journal with the full run log and captures an important workflow fix for Qodo review behavior: allowing the review bot to react to pushes made by `claude[bot]` on `agent/*` branches. It documents the complete end-to-end debugging story from the failed and ambiguous runs through the successful agent execution, the review finding, the fix commit, and the remaining human step required to get Qodo to re-review that bot-authored push.

## Why this PR was created

The main problem being addressed is that Qodo was **not re-reviewing bot-authored pushes** on agent branches, even though it had been reviewing human pushes promptly. In practice, this broke the intended “fix → push → re-review” loop for the agent workflow:

- Human pushes triggered Qodo reviews as expected.
- A fix pushed by `claude[bot]` on an `agent/*` branch did **not** automatically trigger Qodo.
- The review only happened after a human manually commented `/review`.

This PR records that behavior and adjusts repository configuration so Qodo can see those bot pushes in the future, reducing manual intervention and making the agent review loop work as intended.

It also preserves the full journaled evidence from Day 4, including:
- the zombie run during the GitHub Actions incident,
- the missing GitHub App installation,
- the agent-mode no-op,
- the working run,
- the Qodo finding,
- the `@claude` fix,
- and the manual `/review` step.

## What changed

### 1) Added `.pr_agent.toml`
A new repository-level Qodo configuration file was introduced to change bot-handling behavior:

- `ignore_bot_pr = false`
- `push_trigger_ignore_bot_commits = false`

These settings are applied under both:
- `[github]`
- `[github_app]`

This ensures the configuration works across variants of the app/server behavior and addresses the fact that some versions may read one section or the other. The comment block in the file explains the rationale and documents the Day 4 finding.

### 2) Expanded `journal/day-04.md`
The Day 4 journal was updated with:
- a detailed timeline table covering the successful run, PR creation, review finding, fix push, and the missing auto re-review,
- notes about the manual verification steps,
- a new “What still needed me” section that clearly separates deliberate human actions from automation,
- a refined lesson section describing the operational takeaway,
- and updated evidence links for the workflows, runs, and PRs involved.

## Files modified

- `.pr_agent.toml` — new Qodo review configuration
- `journal/day-04.md` — expanded journal narrative, evidence, and lesson learned

## Areas affected

### Review automation / Qodo integration
This PR affects how Qodo processes:
- PR events from bot senders,
- push events containing bot-authored commits,
- and review re-triggering on agent branch updates.

### Agent workflow behavior
It impacts the agent branch flow where:
- `claude[bot]` makes a fix commit,
- the branch is expected to be re-reviewed automatically,
- and human intervention should ideally be minimized.

### Project documentation / operational journal
The `journal/day-04.md` file now documents the run history, troubleshooting, and final learning in more detail, making the process reproducible and auditable for future runs.

## Net result

This PR both **documents** the Day 4 workflow findings and **configures the repository** so Qodo can re-review bot pushes on `agent/*` branches, closing the fix-and-re-review gap that previously required a manual `/review` comment.

pull_requests.title: feat(render): add --origin, link base from the origin remote without its credentials (T-010)
pull_requests.description:
Closes #25

Ticket: tickets/T-010-repo-url-from-origin.md

`render --origin` builds commit and PR links from `git remote get-url origin`. It is opt-in and
offline: without the flag git never runs. Accepts https, ssh:// and `user@host:owner/repo`
remotes. Credentials are dropped and never printed, in the output or in any error.

- New `src/remote.ts`: `repoUrlFromRemote()`, pure, result always passes `checkRepoUrl()`.
- `src/cli.ts`: `--origin`, `CliIo.readOrigin` (default `execFileSync('git', …)`, no shell).
- AGENTS.md rule 6: framing list names the `.git` suffix and userinfo of a git remote.
- Tests: 291 (227 before). Git runs only in throwaway repos under the OS temp dir, with
  inherited `GIT_*` variables removed.

Local Qodo review: 3 deep rounds, then gate NOT MET. 9 findings: 6 fixed, 3 dismissed by the
human. Last one (f1cdda45, test rows) fixed under a one-off exception; this PR's review is the
first review of the final tree. Evidence: evidence/day11/.

generated_descriptions.short_why: Add an opt-in way to build commit and PR links from the local git origin remote, so rendered output can use the repository base URL without requiring credentials or network access.
generated_descriptions.short_how: Added a new remote URL parsing module, wired a `--origin` flag into the CLI with a safe `git remote get-url origin` reader, updated framing/rules around git remote formatting, and added tests covering supported remote formats and credential stripping in temporary git repos.

generated_descriptions.long:
This PR implements the T-008 config-file work for **ignore patterns only**, while also introducing the project’s new **quality gate** workflow and adjusting planning/documentation to match the narrowed scope.

## Why this PR was created

The original T-008 backlog item covered a `.tracenotes.json` config file with both **ignore patterns** and **custom section names**. During implementation, that ticket was split so this PR focuses only on the ignore-pattern part, with section names moved out to a new ticket (**T-027**).

The PR solves a few related problems:

- Adds a way to configure commit filtering through `--config <path>`.
- Lets users ignore commits by pattern instead of only by built-in rules like merge commits.
- Ensures ignored commits are still accounted for correctly in output and versioning logic.
- Tightens CLI behavior so config handling is explicit and predictable.
- Adds a project-level **quality gate** process for agent work, documenting how Qodo findings must be handled.

## How it was implemented

### New config support
A new config system was added to read and validate `.tracenotes.json`-style files with ignore patterns.

Implemented behavior includes:

- strict JSON parsing
- validation of the config shape
- support for an `ignore` array of regex patterns
- rejection of invalid patterns and malformed config structures
- support for BOM handling
- explicit `--config <path>` handling rather than auto-discovery

### CLI changes
The CLI was updated so config can be passed into the commands that need it:

- `group`
- `render`
- `version`

The CLI now also:

- reads the config file through a dedicated loader
- validates config before proceeding
- reports config errors consistently
- enforces option parsing rules for `--config`

### Commit grouping and rendering
The grouping logic was updated so commits can be marked ignored for either:

- merge commits
- matching ignore patterns

Ignored entries now carry a reason, such as:

- `merge commit`
- `ignore pattern: <pattern>`

Rendering was also updated so the output can reflect ignored-by-config commits without changing unrelated output when no config is used.

### Tests and fixtures
New tests were added around config parsing, CLI behavior, and ignore-pattern handling, along with fixture files for valid and invalid config inputs.

### Quality gate workflow and docs
This PR also updates repository process documentation and automation:

- **AGENTS.md** gains a new **Quality gate** section defining how Qodo findings are mapped to severity and handled.
- **.github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml** is updated to require the agent’s final comment to end with **“Implemented, gate pending”** when Qodo cannot be run in that job.
- **BACKLOG.md** is updated to reflect the T-008 split and mark T-008 as done, with T-027 added as a new planned ticket.
- `evidence/day09/*` files were added to record the review and fix-round history.

## Files changed

### Core code
- `src/config.ts` — new config parser and ignore-pattern compiler
- `src/cli.ts` — config loading, `--config` handling, error formatting
- `src/group.ts` — apply ignore patterns during grouping
- `src/render.ts` — rendering updates for ignored commits / closing line
- `src/version.ts` — documentation/comment update related to grouping/version logic
- `src/index.ts` — export updates

### Tests
- `tests/config.test.ts` — new config parser tests
- `tests/cli.test.ts` — CLI behavior and error handling
- `tests/group.test.ts` — grouping behavior with ignore patterns
- `tests/render.test.ts` — render output cases
- `tests/version.test.ts` — version logic coverage
- `tests/fixtures/config-*.json` — config fixtures, including BOM and invalid UTF-8 cases

### Process / planning / automation
- `.github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml` — agent comment guidance for quality gate
- `AGENTS.md` — new quality gate rules
- `BACKLOG.md` — T-008 scope update and new T-027 ticket
- `evidence/day09/*` — review evidence and decision logs

## Affected areas of the codebase

This PR touches several areas:

- **Configuration parsing**: new config file support and validation
- **CLI interface**: `--config` option handling and error reporting
- **Commit grouping logic**: ignoring commits by pattern
- **Rendering/output**: how ignored commits are represented
- **Version recommendation logic**: ensuring ignored commits don’t distort version calculations
- **Tests and fixtures**: broad coverage for new config behavior
- **Repo governance/process**: quality gate rules and agent workflow documentation

## Summary

In short, this PR delivers the **ignore-pattern portion** of T-008 by adding explicit config-file support and integrating it into the CLI, grouping, and rendering pipeline. It also formalizes the repository’s new **quality gate** process and updates backlog/planning docs to reflect the ticket split.

pull_requests.title: feat: parse git log streams from stdin (T-002)
pull_requests.description:
## Day 3: feed your agent a ticket

  Implements `tickets/T-002-read-git-log-stream.md`: parse a `git log` stream from stdin into commits with SHA, author, date, and a parsed message. Nine acceptance criteria, written before implementation. The agent built it from the ticket text
  and `AGENTS.md` only.

  ### What's in the change
  - `src/gitlog.ts`: `parseGitLog`. Splits on the record and field separators, validates SHAs, keeps dates as strings with an ISO 8601 shape warning. Invalid SHAs and short records go to a `malformed` list with a reason. `count` always equals
  `commits + malformed`, so nothing in the range is dropped silently.
  - `src/cli.ts`: `tracenotes log` reads the stream from stdin and prints JSON. Exit 0 even with malformed records, exit 2 on empty stdin.
  - `tests/gitlog.test.ts`, `tests/cli.test.ts`: 11 new tests, one per criterion plus edge cases. Two fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`, marked binary in `.gitattributes` so the LF policy leaves the control bytes alone.
  - README: "From git history" section with the pipe command.
  - `journal/day-02.md`: records the Review Standards import (14 rules from AGENTS.md).
  - `journal/day-03.md`: criterion-by-criterion comparison and what the agent missed.

  ### Verification
  `npm run check` passes, 44 tests. The repository's own history piped through `tracenotes log` returns 7 commits and 0 malformed records, from both Git Bash and PowerShell 5.1.

  ### Result against the ticket
  9 of 9 criteria met. The gaps were in the ticket, not the code: it never mentioned the framing newline git prints between records, and it left separator collisions inside a message undefined. Both are documented in the journal.

generated_descriptions.short_why: To support ticket T-002, the project needed to read a `git log` stream from stdin and turn it into structured commit data for the agent to consume, while handling malformed input predictably.
generated_descriptions.short_how: Added `parseGitLog` in `src/gitlog.ts` to split and validate git log records, report malformed SHAs/short records, and preserve commit counts; updated `src/cli.ts` so `tracenotes log` reads from stdin and outputs JSON with the required exit behavior; added tests and fixtures for parser/CLI edge cases; and updated the README and journaling files with usage and implementation notes.
